cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Prove Your Loyalty
cards.instruction: Invent small tests of loyalty and judge every response without admitting there is a test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. Which photo should go on the reunion poster? Mine or Sam's?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam's is sharper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. Sharpness first. Would you at least show the committee mine first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send both together. Same size.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Equal treatment. After three weekends helping you move. Could mine at least be the attachment they open first? Just readability.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For a wedding cake, we weigh the flour. Please put that mug down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's quicker. I've used three mugs already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right. Show me the mug, and I'll weigh one mugful.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I used three different mugs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Please fetch all three. Apparently we're measuring the crockery before we can measure the flour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm tuning this piano. Please leave the keys alone while I listen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm checking the sticky ones so you can fix those too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Mark them with these little stickers. Silently, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Done. Shall I peel them off so you can play?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One at a time. After I reach each key. We've nearly invented a system.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which photo should go on the reunion poster? Mine or Sam's?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam's is sharper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sharpness first. Would you at least show the committee mine first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send both together. Same size.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Equal treatment. After three weekends helping you move. Could mine at least be the attachment they open first? Just readability.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you keep Friday free? I might need help moving.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've promised to help Alex paint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. Paint takes priority. Could you at least leave your phone on?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. Have you actually found a flat?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Still looking. Nice that I'm worth a charged battery. This is just planning.

cards.title: The Only Professional

cards.title: Give It Up
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. Let me have the medal for the charity auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. Then it should raise more than the toaster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I lend it for the display? I still want people to know I won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then present it to the buyer yourself. I'll print your name in the programme; everyone will know whose medal was worth giving up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would you sell your signed guitar so we can replace the fridge?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I queued all night for that signature.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sell the case. The guitar stays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the case. You can still tell the queue story while I photograph the guitar.

beats.text: The bakery can't sell your cake, love. They think it's too special to slice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says 'inedible.' I thought I'd finally found something I was good at.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You have. Display cakes aren't meant to be eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll ask them to put it in the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me ask. I'll explain the display concept before they get confused again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The magazine hasn't rejected your poem. They think it deserves its own booklet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They returned it. If even you think it's hopeless, I'll stop writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's why they returned it. They can't give it enough space.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you write that on the cover? With your name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. 'A voice that deserves more space.' Print my name large enough for the editor to see.
